As discussed:

1) empty oil from tank where you can see the bottom

2) make sure agitator is turned 90 degrees (matching green mark above)

3) if you can see chocolate on the bottom put 1-2 inches of oil in tank and push chocolate over to the drain at the bottom (if we see chocolate on the bottom of the agitator then we assume it is hardened). 

4) fill with 25% HSY ZS chocolate and push oil out of pipe before decrystallizer

5) circulate ZS chocolate and put system in night mode

5) only fill Marcos tank to 25% with chocolate as we may drain all chocolate out into barrels on Monday and refill with fresh ZS chocolate after I talk to Preston Tregaskis

6) post all LPNs on the L3 Prod and IMS chats for the chocolate and we will need Nidia Lopez Corea to put in the system when she wakes up today.

Matt Salt is being added to this product prior to going to the buffer tank.

Since the Amp check shows it is correct I believe that the salt is affecting the flow rate going though the system.

Talking to Alan the temperatures are matching prior run rates however return flow is not.  That’s what makes me think that the salt is changing the flow rate.

Same temperature, lower flow rate, would result in the temper unit freezing up and the scrapper stopping 

My instructions to Alan was to increase the riser pump speed.  

If the team sees a lower temper reading adjust the riser pump to run 50 kg/ h faster instead of raising the temperatures as the normal process would require 

Do you have any other suggestions?
